Moral Foundations Theory is a framework that separates human morality into the following categories:

  - Care/Harm: related to our long evolution as mammals with attachment systems
    and an ability to feel (and dislike) the pain of others. It underlies the
    virtues of kindness, gentleness, and nurturance.

  - Loyalty/Betrayal: related to our long history as tribal creatures able to
    form shifting coalitions. It is active anytime people feel that it is "one
    for all and all for one." It underlies the virtues of patriotism and
    self-sacrifice for the group.

  - Authority/Subversion: shaped by our long primate history of hierarchical
    social interactions. It underlies virtues of leadership and followership,
    including deference to prestigious authority figures and respect for
    traditions.

  - Sanctity/Purity: shaped by the psychology of disgust and contamination. It
    underlies notions of striving to live in an elevated, less carnal, more
    noble, and more "natural" way (often present in religious narratives). This
    foundation underlies the widespread idea that the body is a temple that can
    be desecrated by immoral activities and contaminants (an idea not unique to
    religious traditions). It underlies the virtues of self-discipline,
    self-improvement, naturalness, and spirituality.

  - Equality: related to our intuitions about equal treatment and equal outcome
    for individuals.

  - Proportionality: related to our intuitions about individuals getting
    rewarded in proportion to their merit or contribution.

Every category has a bidirectional nature. For example:

One person's sensitivity to the Care/Harm foundation may lead them to support high levels of immigration from poorer nations, to reduce the suffering of those who migrate. Whereas another person's sensitivity to the very same foundation may lead them to oppose those levels, because they believe it could lead to people they care about being harmed.

# Summary of 2024 Electoral Manifesto

This manifesto outlines a comprehensive plan for national renewal focused on economic stability, improved public services, and constitutional reform.

## Economic Framework

The document establishes strict fiscal rules requiring day-to-day costs to be met by revenues and debt to fall as a share of the economy by the fifth year of forecasts. Central to the economic plan is an industrial strategy featuring a statutory Industrial Strategy Council, a National Wealth Fund capitalised at £7.3 billion, and planning reform to deliver 1.5 million new homes.

The approach emphasises partnership between government, business, and trade unions. Key proposals include replacing business rates with a fairer system, reforming workplace pensions, maintaining corporation tax at 25%, and establishing Skills England to coordinate workforce development.

## Energy and Environment

A central commitment involves achieving clean power by 2030 through a new publicly-owned energy company headquartered in Scotland. The plan includes doubling onshore wind, tripling solar power, and quadrupling offshore wind. The manifesto proposes investing £8.3 billion in this company while also committing £6.6 billion for home energy efficiency upgrades.

Environmental measures include stricter water company regulation, creation of new national river walks and forests, and stronger animal welfare protections.

## Public Services

Healthcare reforms focus on reducing NHS waiting times through 40,000 additional weekly appointments, doubling CT and MRI scanners, recruiting 8,500 mental health staff, and reforming dentistry with 700,000 additional urgent appointments. The manifesto commits to developing a National Care Service with uniform standards.

Education proposals include recruiting 6,500 new teachers, establishing 3,000 nurseries in primary schools, providing free breakfast clubs in all primary schools, and creating specialist Technical Excellence Colleges.

## Security and Justice

Defence commitments include maintaining nuclear deterrent, upholding the commitment to the transatlantic alliance, conducting a Strategic Defence Review, and continuing support for Ukraine. Border security measures propose establishing a new Border Security Command with counter-terrorism powers and hiring additional caseworkers to clear asylum backlogs.

Criminal justice reforms emphasise neighbourhood policing with thousands of new officers, halving knife crime within a decade, and establishing specialist units in every police force for serious sexual offences.

## Constitutional Reform

Proposed changes include establishing an Ethics and Integrity Commission, removing hereditary peers from the upper legislative chamber, introducing mandatory retirement at 80 for that chamber, and extending voting rights to 16-17 year-olds. The manifesto commits to strengthening devolution through a new Council of Nations and Regions and improved intergovernmental cooperation.

## Employment and Equality

Worker protections include banning exploitative zero-hour contracts, ending fire-and-rehire practices, establishing day-one employment rights, and creating a Fair Pay Agreement for adult social care. The manifesto proposes a Race Equality Act and measures to reduce gender, disability, and ethnicity pay gaps.

## International Relations

Foreign policy priorities include resetting European relationships while remaining outside the single market and customs union, seeking new trade agreements aligned with industrial strategy, pursuing climate leadership through a Clean Power Alliance, and restoring international development spending to 0.7% of gross national income when fiscal circumstances allow.

This document outlines a comprehensive policy platform focused on economic stability, public services, security, and social welfare.

## Economic Policy

The document emphasises fiscal responsibility, citing reduced inflation and returning growth as evidence of economic recovery following pandemic and energy-related challenges. Key proposals include:

- Halving employee National Insurance from 12% to 6% by April 2027
- Abolishing the main rate of self-employed National Insurance

- Maintaining current corporation tax rates and business investment incentives
- Expanding childcare to 30 free hours weekly from nine months old

## Immigration and Border Control

The document proposes:
- A legally binding annual cap on migration
- Removal of illegal migrants to deter irregular crossings
- Working internationally to reform asylum treaties
- Raising income thresholds for skilled worker and family visas

## Defence and Security

Commitments include:
- Increasing defence spending to 2.5% of GDP by 2030
- Supporting continued assistance to Ukraine
- Modernising armed forces with emphasis on technology and innovation
- Investing £10 billion in domestic munitions production

## Public Services

Healthcare proposals include increased NHS spending above inflation, recruiting 92,000 additional nurses and 28,000 doctors, expanding community diagnostic centres, and improving mental health provision.

## Housing and Infrastructure

The document targets 1.6 million new homes, prioritising brownfield development, maintaining green belt protections, and abolishing stamp duty for first-time buyers on properties up to £425,000.

## Environment and Energy

The approach balances net zero commitments with energy security, supporting continued North Sea extraction, nuclear expansion, and renewable investment while opposing immediate transitions that burden households.
